forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred to the southeast will continue to move eastwards over Victoria and over the Tasman Sea on Tuesday. This high will continue to extend a ridge westwards over SA ahead of a low pressure trough that is expected to move over the far west of SA during Wednesday. The trough will slip southeastwards over southern coasts during Thursday and Friday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Cold at first with patchy frost about the agricultural area. Dry and mostly sunny day. Maximum temperatures above average in the north and west but slightly below average elsewhere. Southeast to northeasterly winds. Afternoon sea breezes near the coast.
Dry apart from a possible isolated thunderstorm near the northern border in the far northwest. Areas of raised dust in the northeast. South to southeasterly winds.

Cold at first about eastern districts with with patchy frost. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms developing in the far southwest and in the far northeast corner. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average in the west. Southeast to northeasterly winds ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the southwest in the evening.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far southwest and the chance of an isolated shower about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the west.

text.p: Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far southwest and the chance of an isolated shower about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending fresh at times in the north, ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change about the southwest and southern parts.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: Generally less than 2 mm about the far west and southern coasts, with local falls of 2 to 5 mm possible.
